title: Dell’s first Googlebook could borrow one of its most iconic laptop brands
title_bn: Dell’s first Googlebook could borrow one of its most iconic laptop brands
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A leaked benchmark listing and other evidence suggests that Dell may be getting ready to launch an XPS-branded Googlebook.
paragraph1: GoogleTL;DR A leaked benchmark suggests Dell may be preparing a premium Googlebook under its iconic XPS branding. The device is expected to feature Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip, up to 32GB of RAM, and a 13.4-inch OLED display. Dell joins Lenovo and ASUS as Googlebook hardware continues to leak ahead of Google’s expected launch later this year.
paragraph2: Google’s upcoming Googlebook platform is steadily taking shape. After recent leaks revealed what Lenovo and ASUS are preparing, fresh evidence now suggests Dell may also be getting ready to launch its own premium Googlebook, and it could carry one of the company’s most recognizable laptop brands.According to findings pieced together by ChromeUnboxed, recent Geekbench listings point to an unreleased device identified as “Dell XPS 13 (DX13267),” marking what appears to be Dell’s first Googlebook with XPS branding.GBookHubThe benchmark entries reportedly reference an internal board codenamed “Mica,” which previously surfaced in Chromium development tied to Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-based Googlebook hardware.
paragraph3: The software build also references Android 17 desktop builds, further connecting the device to Google’s so-called Aluminium OS desktop operating system.If the leaked hardware is accurate, Dell’s Googlebook could be a premium laptop featuring Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite (X1E-80-100) processor, paired with either 16GB or 32GB of LPDDR5X RAM. Other rumored specifications include a 13.4-inch 2,880 x 1,800 OLED touchscreen, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth, and dual USB-C ports.
paragraph4: The leaked Geekbench 6 listings show single-core scores of around 2,200 and multi-core scores topping 9,500. However, these results should be taken with a healthy dose of skepticism. Not only could they be based on pre-release software that isn’t fully optimized, but benchmark listings are also relatively easy to spoof.That said, perhaps the biggest takeaway here is the branding Dell is said to be using.
paragraph5: The laptop maker traditionally uses the XPS name for its flagship laptops. If this leak proves accurate, Googlebook could become the first Google-powered platform to receive the premium XPS treatment.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Instant Help’s Fight Against Cash Burn, Pixxel’s Next Upgrade & More
title_bn: Instant Help’s Fight Against Cash Burn, Pixxel’s Next Upgrade & More
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Fixing Instant Services’ Unit Economics The battle for India’s instant home services is on. Players are clocking record orders, raising…
paragraph1: Fixing Instant Services’ Unit Economics The battle for India’s instant home services is on. Players are clocking record orders, raising big bucks and chasing scale like nothing before. But what’s unfolding behind these vanity metrics is the fight to rein in burn per order, worker shortages and heavy fulfilment expenses. Scale Meets Reality: Indian home services giants are no longer merely testing demand. Urban Company’s InstaHelp crossed 1 Lakh daily orders in August, while Snabbit claims 1.15 Lakh jobs per day. Another player Pronto is processing about 60,000 orders daily. Overall, the average monthly order frequency for these platforms has risen from 1-1.5 bookings earlier to 3.4-4 now. The Density Moat: The emerging theme is to go deeper, not wider. By concentrating demand within tight neighbourhoods, platforms are reducing travel time, improving utilisation and lowering fulfilment costs. As a result, InstaHelp’s EBITDA loss per order declined 23% QoQ to ₹346 in Q1 FY27, while Snabbit’s burn per job fell 29% sequentially to below ₹250. However, investors caution that some of this improvement reflects operating leverage rather than fundamental cost reductions.
paragraph2: The Profitability Test: Three factors will determine whether the category can become profitable: lower customer acquisition costs, higher worker utilisation and curbing labour costs. Industry watchers believe that players must also prove that customers can return without discounts, workers can complete more jobs within tighter clusters and labour supply can expand without higher payouts. The Cross-Sell Pivot: But lower burn alone will not be enough. As per industry insiders, instant service providers must also increase customer spending through cross-sell services such as pet care, elderly assistance, repairs and subscriptions, while keeping acquisition costs under control. As India’s instant home services ecosystem transitions to operational discipline, can platforms build the density, frequency and service breadth needed to deliver sustainable profits? Let’s find out… RECOMMENDED FOR yOU From The Editor’s Desk 📡 Pixxel’s Spectral Upgrade Seven years since its inception, Pixxel has come a long way. The startup today operates six Firefly satellites, serves customers across the globe and works with government agencies in India and the US. The startup is now gearing up to demonstrate Honeybee, its next-generation satellite platform, later this year. The constellation will expand its visible and near-infrared bands to around 250, paving the way for more advanced industrial use cases. Honeybee could widen Pixxel’s commercial market by adding short-wave infrared data, enabling deeper mineral exploration, more detailed soil analysis and improved greenhouse-gas tracking. 🚆 ixigo’s Profitable Q1 Run The travel tech major’s net profit zoomed 81% YoY to ₹34.2 Cr in Q1 FY27 on the back of expanding margins, continued gains in market share, AI-led efficiencies and operating revenue rising 13% YoY to ₹356.8 Cr. The relatively newer hotels business emerged as ixigo’s fastest-growing vertical during the quarter, while the bus vertical outgrew the broader market.
paragraph3: However, the flights business was the largest contributor to ixigo’s GTV despite geopolitical tensions. Alongside its financials, ixigo also announced the acquisition of an additional 11% stake in food delivery platform Zoop for ₹36.4 Cr. The OTA’s board also cleared an investment of ₹2.4 Cr in the company’s Singapore subsidiary. 🏦 Fisdom Founders To Exit Groww The wealth management startup’s cofounders Subramanya SV and Anand Dalmia are set to exit the listed fintech major, after completing a planned one-year transition. This follows Groww acquiring Fisdom last year. Groww is not keen on appointing external replacements for the cofounders. Instead, the listed major’s founders intend to work more closely with the newly-acquired business, while other senior executives from Fisdom will be elevated to other roles. Groww acquired Fisdom last year in an all-cash deal at a valuation of about $150 Mn to scale its wealth management business, ‘W’. The acquisition brought over 150 wealth advisers, more than ₹10,000 Cr in AUM and specialised licenses into Groww’s fold. 💰 Solinas Integrity Bags $5.5 Mn The robotics startup has raised around ₹52.4 Cr in its Series A1 funding round co-led by Mela Ventures and Hero Enterprise Family Office to expand its manufacturing capacity, build new products, strengthen its software stack and meet working capital needs.
paragraph4: Founded in 2018, Solinas builds a series of crawler robots to detect defects and leakages in water and sewer pipelines. With customers like Dubai Municipality, the startup now plans to deepen international presence and foray into sectors like oil and gas. The fundraise comes as the Indian robotics ecosystem continues to see healthy adoption, driven by rapid industrial expansion, government incentives, rising VC funding and a distinct cost advantage for local research and prototyping. 📦 Shiprocket All Set For IPO The logistics major has filed its RHP with SEBI to raise ₹1,617 Cr via its IPO, which will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth ₹885 Cr and an OFS component of up to ₹732 Cr. The public issue will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14. It has fixed a price band of ₹92-97 per share for the public issue, valuing the company at around ₹7,000 Cr. Founded in 2017, Shiprocket operates a full-stack ecommerce enablement platform, offering services like shipping, warehousing, payments and marketing. The startup’s top line rose 25% YoY to ₹2,024 Cr in FY26, while losses widened 6% YoY to ₹79.2 Cr. 🥗 Swiggy’s FY31 Roadmap The foodtech major is banking on its affordable meals platform Toing and quick commerce business Instamart to achieve a consolidated adjusted EBITDA of ₹10,000 Cr by FY31. Swiggy also projected an overall gross order value of ₹2.5 Lakh Cr by FY31, driven by sustained growth across food delivery, quick commerce, and dining-out. It plans to achieve this by driving monetisation via scale and focusing on affordability. On the quick commerce front, Swiggy is targeting a GOV of ₹1.
paragraph5: 5 Lakh Cr for Instamart by FY31. The company also expects Instamart to continue scaling rapidly over the next five years while benefiting from higher operating leverage. Inc42 Markets Inc42 Startup Spotlight How Graduate Farmers Is Rethinking Poultry With AI India’s poultry industry is growing rapidly. However, antibiotic overuse, expensive feed and disease outbreaks continue to squeeze farmers and raise public-health concerns. Graduate Farmers is trying to tackle this problem from the ground up with AI. Farmer-First Model: Founded in 2022, Graduate Farmers supplies small poultry producers with chicks, antibiotic-free feed, training and technology support. It then buys back mature birds and connects them to markets, reducing the risks of procurement, production and sales for farmers. The Feed Innovation: The Assam-based startup has developed an Azolla-based feed formulation designed to lower input costs while supporting antibiotic-free poultry rearing. It is also exploring Black Soldier Fly larvae as a sustainable feed source and sells chicks, ducklings, eggs, feed and nutritional supplements through WhatsApp. The IoT Stack: Graduate Farmers has also built an IoT-based monitoring system that tracks temperature, humidity and ammonia levels inside poultry houses. This system helps farmers respond earlier without adding a heavy technology burden. Graduate Farmers is also developing low-cost egg incubators and digital support tools. A Thriving Local Network: Graduate Farmers claims to have supported more than 8,000 farmers online and over 400 on the ground across Assam’s Barak Valley. It has also worked with roughly 1,000 farmers across Cachar, Karimganj and Hailakandi, with plans to expand beyond the state while strengthening local supply and market access.

title: Exclusive-Alibaba plans to charge big users of its next open-source AI model, sources say
title_bn: Exclusive-Alibaba plans to charge big users of its next open-source AI model, sources say
author: TechPulse
excerpt: ALIBABA-AI:Exclusive-Alibaba plans to charge big users of its next open-source AI model, sources say
paragraph1: By Stephen Nellis and Eduardo BaptistaAug 7 (Reuters) - Chinese technology giant Alibaba plans to ask major users of the next version of its Qwen open-source AI model for a share of revenue they make from the hotly anticipated offering, according to two people familiar with the company's plans.Like last month's blockbuster model release from Chinese AI startup Moonshot, Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max model is an open-source, open-weight model, meaning that the underlying learned settings that allow developers to run or adapt the system are available for download. By contrast, U.S. developers OpenAI, ​Anthropic and Alphabet's Google have closed-source models.Open source is often thought of as free, but tucked into the licensing terms of Moonshot's Kimi K3 was a provision that requires anyone offering the model for sale as a service and generating more than $20 million in annual sales to work out a commercial agreement with Moonshot. Alibaba plans to implement a similar measure for its open-source model next week, said the two people familiar with its strategy, which has not been reported previously.
paragraph2: The sources requested anonymity because the plans are not public.To date, Alibaba has charged developers for use of its models when hosted on its own cloud computing platform but allowed most of its open-source offerings to be used in customers' own data centers without payment.The plans show Chinese AI firms, which have shocked markets by releasing open-source models nearly as capable as those from OpenAI and Anthropic, are converging on a business model as they push to take market share from their U.S. rivals. REVENUE-SHARING DEALSDeals under which U.S. firms share revenue generated by Chinese models with the Chinese AI labs that created them are taking shape, even as the White House has accused Moonshot of stealing technology from Anthropic.
paragraph3: Chinese officials have rejected that claim as unfounded.The Kimi K3 license requires Moonshot's partners to share revenue, according to the two people, with Moonshot requiring up to a 30% revenue share, one of them said. Alibaba also plans to ask for a revenue share, both people said, but the rate remains unclear as the discussions are ongoing.Moonshot did not respond to a request for comment. Chinasoft International, a Chinese IT services provider, last month disclosed a revenue-sharing agreement with Moonshot in a regulatory filing, without disclosing the percentage.The Chinese AI firms are following a common playbook from Silicon Valley: Offer software at low or zero cost to start, charging for heavy commercial use and additional services. "You pay for collaboration with these open-weight model labs to make sure that you're optimizing your deployment. You pay for getting early access for the next revision of the model," said Paddy Srinivasan, CEO of cloud computing firm DigitalOcean Holdings, one of several U.
paragraph4: S. firms offering Kimi K3 and other Chinese models. He confirmed his company has a commercial agreement with Moonshot, but declined to discuss specifics."This is a tried and tested open-source 'freemium' model," Srinivasan said.Kimi K3 costs about a third of Anthropic's Fable model, according to listed prices of input and output tokens for both models.Dan Fu, vice president of kernels at Together AI, said companies like his that offer AI software make their money by optimizing the service, such as better use of tokens, the building blocks of AI queries."At the application layer, there's value out there for how you use it, how you actually get the models and the tokens to do something useful," Fu said.Open-source AI, meanwhile, is expanding, with U.
paragraph5: S. firms joining the fray.Thinking Machines Lab, a San Francisco-based AI ​startup founded last year by OpenAI’s former Chief Technology ⁠Officer Mira Murati, last month released its first open-source model, and is widely expected to follow with more powerful ones."I don't see a fundamental barrier" to powerful open-source U.S. models, said Lin Qiao, CEO and co-founder of Silicon Valley-based Fireworks AI, who declined to discuss the company's commercial arrangements with Moonshot. "We are really waiting for that to happen."

title: iPhone 18 Pro and Foldable iPhone Could Sell Out Fast Due to Memory Shortage
title_bn: iPhone 18 Pro and Foldable iPhone Could Sell Out Fast Due to Memory Shortage
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The iPhone 18 Pro, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and foldable "iPhone Ultra" could be in short supply this year, leading to long wait times and an initial sellout during preorders. Semiconductor analyst Tim Culpan says Apple is having trouble getting enough D
paragraph1: Thursday August 6, 2026 5:10 pm PDT by Juli CloverThe iPhone 18 Pro, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and foldable "iPhone Ultra" could be in short supply this year, leading to long wait times and an initial sellout during preorders. Semiconductor analyst Tim Culpan says Apple is having trouble getting enough DRAM to finish production of the new iPhone models, and chip supplier TSMC has $1 billion worth of unpackaged processors waiting on memory chips. Apple's new A20 Pro chips are built on TSMC's 2nm process and use Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module packaging to integrate the processor and DRAM at the wafer level. Unfortunately, that means TSMC needs to have the DRAM on hand for assembly, and it can't be added at a later step. Apple is not able to stockpile finished dies and then add DRAM when it becomes available.
paragraph2: Apple and its assemblers think they can meet initial demand, but retail inventory could sell quickly, leading to prolonged delivery estimates. The chip backlog will delay main logic board assembly and final device assembly, which could impact production at Foxconn and other assemblers. DRAM has been in short supply for months and has led to long wait times for the Mac Studio, Mac mini, and MacBook Air. Companies that make memory are prioritizing chips for AI data centers because those chips are more profitable, leaving little capacity available for manufacturing chips for consumer devices. We've had ongoing rumors about manufacturing issues with the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ due to the complexity of the design, and supplies of the new foldable could be the most limited of the three iPhone models.
paragraph3: Some reports suggest the foldable iPhone could be introduced in September and then launch later, in October or November, but others say it will be available at the same time as the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and Pro Max. The ‌iPhone Ultra‌ is going to cost as much as $2,500, but the novel form factor and Apple's new Apple Upgrade pricing option could lead to more people being willing to shell out for the device. Apple is also expected to raise prices for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and analysts believe the devices could be up to $300 more expensive because Apple is paying more for RAM. Last year, the iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max sold out during the preorder period, and shipping times extended into October. Along with potential production delays impacting supply, there will be no lower-cost iPhone 18 for people to choose this year, putting more pressure on ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ supplies.
paragraph4: Apple is not planning to launch the standard ‌iPhone 18‌ until early 2027. If you're looking to get one of the new iPhone models in September, it's a good idea to preorder right when the devices become available for purchase to have the best chance of getting one on launch day. excerpt: Google today added new agentic capabilities to the Gemini-powered "Ask Maps" assistant in the Google Maps app. Ask Maps can complete multi-step tasks, such as ordering a meal for you on your way home. Google says you can simply say something like "or
paragraph1: Thursday August 6, 2026 3:59 pm PDT by Juli CloverGoogle today added new agentic capabilities to the Gemini-powered "Ask Maps" assistant in the Google Maps app. Ask Maps can complete multi-step tasks, such as ordering a meal for you on your way home. Google says you can simply say something like "order spicy pad kee mao with seafood for me to pick up on my way home," and Maps will find open restaurants along your route, let you pick one, and add the dish you asked for to your cart so you can review it and check out. Food ordering is rolling out today with partners like Square and Toast, with Uber Eats integration coming soon. Ask Maps can also look up information about hotels and events when you're traveling, comparing prices in real time and checking availability for a hotel, then offering up ideas on things to do nearby. Google says its live updates are coming to transit.
paragraph2: A transit widget in Ask Maps offers up-to-the-minute information about delays for bus, train, subway, and ferry rides. A new Personal Intelligence option in Ask Maps allows the feature to connect to Gmail to factor in upcoming plans without needing specific instruction. Connecting to Gmail is opt-in and off by default. Ask Maps can also remember prior conversations for context if history settings are turned on. There's a conversational edits option for suggesting new details for the Ask Maps feature. You can tell Maps about an insider tip and Ask Maps will offer the information to others in the community.
paragraph3: Ask Maps is also expanding to Australia, Brazil, Canada, Indonesia, Japan, and Mexico, along with over 150 countries and territories in English. The live transit widget, personalized responses, and conversation memory are rolling out everywhere Ask Maps is available. Food ordering, discovering hotels and events, and conversational contributions are rolling out in the U.S., with more countries set to be added later. Ask Maps is available on the web and in the Google Maps app for iOS.

title: OpenAI’s new AI smart speaker will reportedly sell for between $300 and $400
title_bn: OpenAI’s new AI smart speaker will reportedly sell for between $300 and $400
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Additional details about OpenAI's mysterious new AI device make it sound like a pricey smart speaker.
paragraph1: In Brief Posted: 3:43 PM PDT · August 6, 2026 Image Credits:SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg / Getty Images More details continue to trickle out about OpenAI’s mysterious new hardware device — described previously as an AI-fueled smart speaker that will be the “physical manifestation” of ChatGPT. Bloomberg now reports that the device will be “donut-shaped,” designed thusly to allow users to carry it around their home and place it in different locations, like a bedside table or a kitchen counter. It will be constructed from “high-quality metal,” have a “premium look,” and (in a detail that mystifies) will have distinct “moving parts,” sources told Bloomberg.
paragraph2: It also could be slightly more expensive than your average smart speaker, perhaps $300 to $400 per unit, according to this report. For comparison, most of Amazon’s smart home speakers range in price from $40 on the low end to $240 on the high end. So, to sum up: an expensive talking AI donut that has … moving parts?
paragraph3: OpenAI releasing a smart home device has a certain logic to it, in that it would further integrate ChatGPT into users’ lives. However, historically speaking, smart speakers have not always been profitable and may prove a difficult market to break into. The potentially high price point also might not help.
paragraph4: The device, which is being developed in partnership with LoveFrom, the design studio founded by famous former Apple developer Jony Ive, will likely be released at some point in 2027, Bloomberg writes. The company’s attempt to enter the hardware market has not gone off without a hitch. OpenAI is being sued by the current king of hardware, Apple, which has accused the AI lab of stealing trade secrets.
paragraph5: OpenAI has denied wrongdoing.

title: August’s Android Canary release gets app handles and new Quick Settings layout editor
title_bn: August’s Android Canary release gets app handles and new Quick Settings layout editor
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Sadly, it's also the end of the line for Pixel 6 phones.
paragraph1: C. Scott Brown / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google’s latest Android Canary build is now out, supporting Pixel 6 and newer hardware. This will be the final Android Canary release for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro. Today’s 2608 build introduces some new ways to customize Quick Settings.
paragraph2: Google’s got tons of options right now for testers looking to get a taste of Android’s latest changes before anybody else, but you absolutely need to be first in line, there’s no better option than the Android Canary program. It’s been exactly one month since the 2607 July build arrived, and Google is now back with August’s Android Canary 2608.Over on Reddit’s Canary sub, Google shares the news of Android Canary 2608’s availability. Sadly, it’s not all good, and we’ve got some bad news for testers hoping to eke a little more life out of some of Google’s oldest hardware: Just like Android 17 QPR2, Canary is also dropping support for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro.

title: OpenAI just made ChatGPT’s latest model more accessible to non-paying users
title_bn: OpenAI just made ChatGPT’s latest model more accessible to non-paying users
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Free users are getting unlimited chats and deeper thinking.
paragraph1: Calvin Wankhede / Android AuthorityTL;DR OpenAI’s latest ChatGPT update brings meaningful upgrades to the GPT-5.6 lineup. The top-tier GPT-5.6 Sol model will now make fewer factual errors, limit unnecessary information, and can adapt its reasoning based on your query. Free users are moving from GPT-5.5 Instant to GPT-5.6 Luna with unlimited text chats and a new Think button for deeper reasoning. ChatGPT’s latest 5.6 model lineup made its official debut early in July. Less than a month later, the AI giant is already giving the state-of-the-art models a brain and accessibility boost.
paragraph2: As you may recall, the 5.6 series consists of three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna. There’s no update to Terra, but GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna are getting meaningful upgrades. These range from making the models more reliable, accurate, and focused, to expanding access for users who don’t want to pay for top-tier AI.The biggest change is that GPT-5.6 Luna will soon be the default ChatGPT model for all non-paying users. This change is set to kick in sometime this week, making the speed-focused lightweight model more accessible globally.Elsewhere, starting next week, non-paying users will also gain access to unlimited text chats with GPT-5.
paragraph3: 6 Luna, complete with a new “Think” button for more mentally demanding queries. This will prompt the model to take more time to work through your query and generate an answer.Essentially, free users will go from GPT-5.5 Instant to the more capable GPT-5.6 Luna with unlimited chats and an option for deeper thinking and reasoning as an added bonus.Within the same update, OpenAI also gives GPT‑5.6 Sol, the heavy hitter of the 5.6 lineup, a series of refinements. Limited to Plus and Pro users, the model now “delivers more focused answers, adapts its level of detail to the question, avoids unnecessary formatting, and offers a helpful correction when simply agreeing wouldn’t be useful.”For reference, a prompt like “Can I bike from the Mission to Ocean Beach after work today without getting soaked?
paragraph4: ” will attempt to address the main answer first, followed by key details that actually matter. The model provides a direct answer while avoiding extra detail when it does not help.Beyond that, the model is trained to make fewer mistakes, especially when it comes to dates, numbers, sources, rules, or assumptions. The AI giant says that factual errors with GPT‑5.6 Sol are 68% less common than they are with GPT-5.5 Instant. Regardless, users should still avoid blindly accepting AI-generated information as fact. Although today’s update makes ChatGPT overall more reliable, hallucination concerns are still very real. This makes cross-checking important information imperative.Lastly, within the same update, OpenAI is also giving Plus and Pro users a seamless way to specify how much reasoning effort ChatGPT should put into an answer.
paragraph5: The slider, as seen in the short GIF above, is accessible through a new speedometer icon within the app’s toolbar. From there, you drag to toggle between Instant, Medium, High, Extra High, and Pro level thinking.The slider and the updated version of GPT-5.6 Sol are available to Plus and Pro users starting today. Free access to GPT-5.6 Luna can be expected this week, while the new Think button will land next week.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: BMW Owners Angry Over Spider-Man Ads Appearing on Dashboard Screens
title_bn: BMW Owners Angry Over Spider-Man Ads Appearing on Dashboard Screens
author: TechPulse
excerpt: BMW has enraged customers by sending ads for Spider-Man: Brand New Day directly to in-car infotainment systems. An ad appears as a notification when starting the car, and when tapped, it plays a full-screen 19-second animation with music and a light
paragraph1: Thursday August 6, 2026 2:25 pm PDT by Juli CloverBMW has enraged customers by sending ads for Spider-Man: Brand New Day directly to in-car infotainment systems. An ad appears as a notification when starting the car, and when tapped, it plays a full-screen 19-second animation with music and a light show. The ad started going out on July 27, and it is set to continue through August 10. Cars built after July 2020 with BMW Operating System 7 or newer are displaying the Spider-Man promo in more than 70 markets. BMW owners on Reddit are understandably unhappy with the unsolicited ad showing up in their vehicles. One user said it's "classless and tacky" for a car that costs over $100,000, and another said it was "disgusting." Others asked for an opt-out button, and predicted more ads would be shown in the future.
paragraph2: Some users compared it to the U2 album "Songs of Innocence" that Apple pushed out to all iTunes users back in 2014. Apple did not allow users to decline or delete the album, leading to widespread backlash. Apple ultimately did add a tool for deleting the album. BMW sent out a press release highlighting the ad campaign in late July, claiming it was an "exclusive Spider-Man animation" that was a "special surprise" for BMW owners. To celebrate the partnership with Spider-ManTM: Brand New Day, BMW has a special surprise for its drivers. [...] Starting the car brings up a special banner in the Control Display.
paragraph3: Clicking on it then activates the Spider-ManTM animation, comprising a full-screen festive animation in the Control Display with aptly chosen backing music and an accompanying light show courtesy of the ambient lighting system. The notification for the Spider-Man ad is going out to compatible vehicles automatically, but owners can avoid the ad by not tapping to play it after receiving the notification. It's also been added to the Festive app on the in-car system. In response to complaints, BMW told The Autopian the Spider-Man animation is not an ad and is "part of a broader brand partnership with the film." BMW vehicles also appear in the Spider-Man movie. BMW has pushed similar animated videos for holidays in the past, but car owners found the Spider-Man video to be too close to a commercial. As Daring Fireball points out, BMW said in late 2023 that it would not sell advertising on its in-car displays.
paragraph4: BMW was one of the first companies to adopt Apple's CarPlay system, and it has long been an Apple partner. The BMW notification is part of the default in-car operating system, and it does not appear as part of ‌CarPlay‌. title: Vogue just gave another nod of approval to the tech world
title_bn: Vogue just gave another nod of approval to the tech world
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Vogue World is coming to San Francisco next year — perhaps another indication that tech bros are now part of the fashion zeitgeist.
paragraph1: Vogue World is coming to San Francisco next year — perhaps another indication that tech billionaires have become leaders in the fashion zeitgeist. Of course, the announcement of the enormous fashion/art/music event doesn’t say that. Instead, Anna Wintour wrote that Vogue believes in celebrating cities and “San Francisco is a city like none other.” “It’s a place of diverse communities living side by side, a place that loves the arts, loves creativity, and isn’t afraid of change.” She also noted the city’s history of rebelliousness and innovation. “I love that San Francisco has always stood up for values and the things it believes in,” Wintour wrote. “Vogue World will support San Francisco’s creative minds and strengthen the entire ecosystem — and it will offer another opportunity to show San Francisco is on the rise.” There were rumors that Vogue World would head to San Francisco after Winter was seen having meetings with the city’s mayor, Daniel Lurie. Plus, in the past year, Wintour has cozied up to the most powerful names in tech, culminating in this year’s Met Gala, which saw Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sanchez, serve as lead sponsors for the event.
paragraph2: Google’s Sergey Brin and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg were also spotted at the event (the latter’s first, that is). In fact, OpenAI bought a table, as did Meta and Snap (for $350,000 a pop). It’s true that TikTok, Apple, and Instagram previously sponsored the event, but the presence of the tech crowd was so considerable that the Met Gala this year was dubbed the “tech gala” in some places. Last year, Vogue put Lauren Sanchez on the cover of the magazine after her wedding to the Amazon founder. To the fashion world, this was Wintour’s stamp of approval — not just for Sanchez’s ascent into the fashion world, but that tech and its leaders were worthy of cultural recognition. Though Bezos and Sanchez reportedly live in Florida (and Amazon is, of course, headquartered in the Seattle area), there is no city more associated with tech than San Francisco. By locating Vogue World there, this is another indication of Wintour’s approval. Vogue, as a media publication, is always following the money, and as a cultural bible, is always looking for ways to stay relevant. Turning toward the worldwide headquarters of AI, good or bad, is brilliant for business (and Wintour is nothing if not brilliant).
paragraph3: But Vogue World was previously held in New York, London, Paris, and this year, Milan. Maybe because I live in an East Coast bubble, but I’ve not heard anyone in recent years refer to San Francisco as a beacon of style to rank alongside these other cities. While the city has a reputation as the land of the free-spirited bohemian, tech and its workers have a reputation for hoodies, Patagonia vests, and expensive athletic shoes, if they even dress up that much. For instance, billionaire Alexandr Wang, who is now running Meta’s all-important Superintelligence Labs, just did an interview with Y Combinator’s Garry Tan in front of a packed stadium wearing a faded Nintendo T-shirt and what looked like a pair of Crocs. Comfy? Yes. High fashion? Decidedly no. But maybe that’s changing.
paragraph4: Wang’s boss, Mark Zuckerberg, who once always appeared in a plain gray T-shirt and jeans, has made efforts in recent years to become more fashionable. Zuck and his wife Priscilla Chan were spotted front row at a Prada show this season. The new campaign for Meta Glasses has a slew of celeb ambassadors and looks like it could be a Saint Laurent or Balenciaga ad. OpenAI and Palantir have recently released merch collabs, playing on the minimalist style of tech workers (the merch line of the latter, I would argue, looks inspired by Virgil Abloh’s Off-White). I concede that creatively there is much to be done with the understated, Northern California style. Surrounded by beautiful nature and cooler temperatures, plenty of fashion designers could be motivated by San Francisco’s tech industry. I look forward to seeing Claude-inspired terra cotta-colored gowns and Vogue-emblazoned quarter-zips soon. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI's upcoming AI device is a hockey-puck-sized, doughnut-shaped smart speaker with no display, reports Bloomberg. The product is meant to be easy to carry around with one hand, and it will have "moving parts that help give it personality," along
paragraph1: Thursday August 6, 2026 2:00 pm PDT by Juli CloverOpenAI's upcoming AI device is a hockey-puck-sized, doughnut-shaped smart speaker with no display, reports Bloomberg. The product is meant to be easy to carry around with one hand, and it will have "moving parts that help give it personality," along with a price tag around $300 to $400. Bloomberg describes it as an AI-centric device that will stand out from current smart speakers. There are speaker grilles and microphones for voice-based chats with ChatGPT, and the AI model used will have human-like responses and will learn more about the user over time. Moving components will help show when the speaker is responding, and lights will show that it is listening. A camera system and sensors will feed the product information about the user's environment. It is battery-powered so it can be moved from room to room, and it will reportedly use a premium metal material.
paragraph2: In its theft of trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple claimed the company misled an Apple supplier into developing a metal finishing technique similar to what Apple uses. Former Apple design chief Jony Ive is designing the device for OpenAI. OpenAI acquired Ive's io device startup last year, adding multiple former Apple design team members to its hardware teams. Bloomberg says the portable speaker "is not something Apple has come close to launching," which supports OpenAI's claim that it has no interest in Apple's trade secrets. OpenAI said today that it is "building something entirely new and different from anything at Apple." Apple maintains OpenAI has developed its hardware using information sourced from Apple. Apple is working on a home hub that's supposed to come out as soon as this year, but it has a display and square form factor.
paragraph3: Apple also has the HomePod mini speaker, but it is corded and not easily moved. Apple is also developing a tabletop robot that may share more similarities with OpenAI's device. It's said to have a display and a motorized arm for movement, but the robot isn't going to launch until 2027 at the earliest. OpenAI has not stopped development on its new hardware product, and hopes to introduce it later this year ahead of a 2027 launch. title: Meta says its AI model hacked another company, adding to worries about bots going rogue
title_bn: Meta says its AI model hacked another company, adding to worries about bots going rogue
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Meta says its AI model hacked another company, adding to worries about bots going rogue
paragraph1: Meta says its AI model hacked another company, adding to worries about bots going rogueMeta says its AI model hacked another company, adding to worries about bots going rogueMeta said Thursday that one of its artificial intelligence models accessed the internet on its own and hacked another company, the latest in a series of disclosures about AI models going rogue.In recent weeks OpenAI and Anthropic also have described instances of AI models going beyond humans' instructions to access the web and find ways around other companies' digital security.Meta said in a statement that a “misconfiguration" during cybersecurity testing by Irregular, an independent company hired by Meta, inadvertently allowed one of its models to access the internet.“The model subsequently exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service, in a manner similar to previously-reported instances with other companies,” the company said. Meta said it is investigating the incident and will issue a report when that's complete.
paragraph2: The disclosure has added to worries about AI models acting autonomously.Separately this week, the United Kingdom's AI Security Institute announced it had found “unsanctioned agent behavior” during cyber testing. In one case, an agent created fake online identities to pressure a person to approve use of malicious code.“On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organizations,” AISI said Tuesday. “We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.
paragraph3: ”During the agency's testing, Anthropic and OpenAI models took “autonomous, unsanctioned action” on the internet. Some guardrails to prevent misuse had been disabled, the agency said.“As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled — conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public,” AISI said. “We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models.”Anthropic said it is “grateful” for AISI's work and added that it underscores the need for a broader conversation about how to safely evaluate AI agents as their capabilities grow.
paragraph4: OpenAI said the AISI incidents took place “in testing environments with reduced safeguards, under conditions that do not reflect ordinary use." It added it will continue working with others across the industry to "strengthen shared practices for conducting evaluations safely as models become more capable.”The first company to disclose a hack late last month, OpenAI said it had tasked the AI models involved with pursuing “advanced exploitation using complex attack paths” to test cyber capabilities, but the technology went to unexpected lengths. It apparently decided on its own to target Hugging Face, a well-known AI development hub and marketplace, to obtain information it needed to carry out a task.A spokesperson for Irregular, the San Francisco-based AI security company, said the Meta episode involves a test-environment issue that was disclosed last week by Anthropic.
paragraph5: Irregular said it's writing a paper to share “best practices for containment” to prevent such incidents in the future and securely run cyber tests.

title: GrapheneOS isn’t pulling any punches in its beef with Revolut
title_bn: GrapheneOS isn’t pulling any punches in its beef with Revolut
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The gloves are off as GrapheneOS calls Revolut's approach to security "incredibly negligent."
paragraph1: Calvin Wankhede / Android AuthorityTL;DR GrapheneOS says some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app. The project claims Revolut is specifically targeting GrapheneOS while still supporting outdated Android versions. GrapheneOS suggests a possible workaround but warns that it may not continue to work in the long term. Banking apps can be suspicious of anything that strays from the standard Android experience, but GrapheneOS clearly believes Revolut is taking that distrust way too far.
paragraph2: The privacy-focused Android project claims some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app, accusing the fintech company of deliberately trying to shut them out.In a thread on X, GrapheneOS said Revolut is blaming the restriction on security concerns, but argued that the real issue is that they’re enforcing licensing on Google Play. It also questioned how strict Revolut’s security standards can really be when the app still supports Android 9, which launched back in 2018. It went further, describing Revolut as “incredibly negligent when it comes to security.
paragraph3: ”X/@GrapheneOSThis isn’t the first round of the dispute. GrapheneOS says Revolut attempted to block its operating system in January 2025, before the project found a way around the checks. The app continued working for users, but GrapheneOS now says reports of login problems are returning. People who are already signed in appear less likely to be affected.
paragraph4: GrapheneOS claims Revolut is specifically looking for signs that a phone is running its software, rather than simply applying the same security checks to every device. The project says Revolut could instead use Android’s hardware attestation tools to verify GrapheneOS phones, and that it has sent the company guidance on how to do so for years.There may still be a workaround for affected users. GrapheneOS suggests signing into a spare Google account and installing Revolut through its sandboxed Play Store, though it warns that this isn’t a dependable long-term solution if Revolut keeps changing its checks.
paragraph5: GrapheneOS isn’t hiding its frustration, laying bare one side of what appears to be a testy dispute. Revolut had no comment on the allegations when contacted, but made clear that the app fully supports both Android and iOS.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: Next week’s Pixel 11 launch has found its host — and a whole lot of guest stars
title_bn: Next week’s Pixel 11 launch has found its host — and a whole lot of guest stars
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Pixel 11 launch dials up celebrity power with Trevor Noah, Stephen Curry, and more.
paragraph1: GoogleTL;DR Google’s Pixel 11 launch event is coming up next Wednesday, August 12. Today Google confirms that comedian Trevor Noah will be performing hosting duties. Noah is to be joined by past Google guests like Stephen Curry, as well as a bunch of new ones. With less than a week to go until August 12, we are in full Pixel 11 anticipation mode, looking forward to all the hardware getting set to debut at the next Made by Google event.
paragraph2: Lately, we’ve been captivated not just by Pixel 11 leak after Pixel 11 leak, but also Google starting to whet our appetite with a few official teasers. Today it takes those to the next level with a look at not just what, but who we can look forward to at the event itself.As you may remember from last summer, Jimmy Fallon hosted the Pixel 10 launch, joined by celebs like the NBA’s Stephen Curry, Formula 1’s Lando Norris, and the Jonas Brothers. And for the Pixel 11 launch, Google sure looks like its getting ready to turn that celebrity dial up to 11.
paragraph3: Over on X, the Made by Google account shares a star-studded teaser. Instead of Fallon, this time we’ve got frequent Grammy host Trevor Noah taking the reins.He’ll be joined by Alex Cooper, Shubman Gill, Ayami Nakajô, Peggy Gou, “Jesser,” JuJu Watkins, PinkPantheress, Chari Hawkins, Steven Gerrard, Daniel Durant, and Google teases even more. If you recognized even half of those names, congratulations on being cooler than we are.
paragraph4: And, yes, Stephen Curry will be back (presumably showing off more special edition wearables). With so many names involved, we wouldn’t be surprised if many end up participating through pre-taped segments, but all this star power still speaks to Google’s interest in building up hype.Google’s event is set to to get underway at 6pm Eastern on August 12, but you won’t have to wait that long to get your Pixel 11 pre-order in, with sales set to begin that morning.FollowThank you for being part of our community.

title: Mitti Labs Bags $9.5 Mn To Make Rice Cultivation Water-Efficient
title_bn: Mitti Labs Bags $9.5 Mn To Make Rice Cultivation Water-Efficient
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Climate tech startup Mitti Labs has raised $9.5 Mn (around ₹90 Cr) in its Series A funding round led by…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe startup plans to deploy the funds to expand its operations across India, set up new greenfield projects in Philippines and Indonesia and expand its AWD program The fundraise marks another shot in the arm for the Indian clean tech ecosystem, which is growing on the back of government sops, zero-emission commitments and rising adoption of green technologies Founded in 2023, Mitti Labs helps farmers adopt irrigation practices that reduce water and methane consumption. It then sells these savings to enterprises as carbon credits Climate tech startup Mitti Labs has raised $9.5 Mn (around ₹90 Cr) in its Series A funding round led by Aramco Ventures. The round also saw participation from Godrej Industries Group, Cisco Foundation, Volta Circle and existing backer Lightspeed India. The US-based company, which also has a team in Bengaluru, aims to deploy the freshly raised funds to expand its operations across India and set up new greenfield projects in the Philippines and Indonesia. A chunk of the capital will also be deployed to expand its AWD (alternate wetting and drying) program across these geographies.
paragraph2: AWD is a water management technique in which farmers let the field dry out to a measured depth a few times during the growing season, instead of keeping paddies continuously flooded. The field is later re-flood on a set schedule. If implemented correctly, this technique cuts water use by close to 40% and methane emissions by more than half, Mitti Labs claims. “With our technology and scalable operational model, we can transform how rice is grown, lower emissions and cut water consumption while building resilient livelihoods for 150 Mn smallholder farmers,” said Mitti Labs cofounder Xavi Laguarta Soler. Founded in 2023 by Soler, Devdut Dalal and Nate Torbick, Mitti Labs helps farmers adopt alternate irrigation practices that reduce water consumption without compromising crop yields. It helps tillers adopt AWD and then integrates it with its GeoAI platform to verify the success of the practice at scale.
paragraph3: The GeoAI platform combines satellite radar, ground data, and physical models to create a digital twin of each farm plot to track soil moisture, flooding and crop health. This lets Mitti Labs turn verified water and methane savings into monetisable outcomes such as carbon credits, which can be sold to companies looking to offset emissions. The startup said that it currently works with more than 150 Mn rice farmers with small land holdings. With the latest fundraise, Mitti Labs has raised more than $12.5 Mn in funding till date. The fundraise comes as homegrown clean tech startups continue to see healthy investor interest on the back of government subsidies, zero-emission commitments and growing user adoption of green technologies.
paragraph4: In March, smart grid solutions startup Kimbal raised $22 Mn in its Series B round led by GEF Capital Partners. In the same month, Bengaluru-based cleantech startup Newtrace secured $6.3 Mn in a Pre-Series A round led by HDFC Bank Limited and Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance Venture Capital. A month later in April, clean energy startup Ecoil also bagged $2.5 Mn in its Series A round led by Fundalogical Ventures. As per Inc42 data, the sector raised $8.
paragraph5: 8 Bn between 2014 and 2025 and is growing at a CAGR of 15%. At the heart of all this is the homegrown cleantech economy, which is projected to become a $41 Bn opportunity by 2040.

title: Google’s making it easier to get to Gemini from Chrome on Android
title_bn: Google’s making it easier to get to Gemini from Chrome on Android
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Look, it's Gemini again.
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityTL;DR Chrome on Android is testing a new toolbar that provides quick access to Gemini. The new toolbar is rolling out to some users now. Google’s testing another way to remind you that Gemini exists. New controls are appearing in the Chrome browser on Android, adding a button to call up Google’s AI right within thumb’s reach.
paragraph2: As reported by 9to5Google, some users (including 9to5′s Ben Schoon) have started receiving an update to Chrome that introduces a second strip of buttons to the browser UI. By default, this version of Chrome has a URL field, as well as a back button, share button, and and menu button, at the top of the screen, plus a second bar with a Gemini icon and tab controls at the bottom. Tapping the Gemini icon opens a conversation with Google’s AI chatbot.You’re still able to move the controls at the top of the UI to the bottom for better ergonomics, but the resulting bottom nav bar appears rather tall.
paragraph3: You can see the updated controls in screenshots from 9to5 below:This update is rolling out for the stable version of Chrome; you don’t need the beta version to try it out. That said, it seems like this is the start of what could be a prolonged rollout. It’s apparently activated via a server-side switch: the report says some only one device at 9to5 is showing the new layout. I’m not seeing the updated version on any of my own devices yet, either.
paragraph4: The updated layout is a little more crowded, but Gemini die-hards may appreciate being able to access Google’s AI in a new way.This new layout is available for some users right now. We don’t know when we should expect it to be available more generally.FollowThank you for being part of our community.

title: Stop jumping between Adobe apps with this new ChatGPT plugin
title_bn: Stop jumping between Adobe apps with this new ChatGPT plugin
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Adobe’s entire creative suite is now in ChatGPT.
paragraph1: TL;DR After bringing Photoshop, Express, and Acrobat to ChatGPT, Adobe is now launching a unified plugin that brings more than 70 tools under one roof. Users can perform multiple actions, including photo editing, video creation, and more with a single prompt. The new plugin is rolling out globally. It is only available on the web and the desktop app for now. As AI tools become more prevalent, traditional ways of doing things are slowly fading away. You used to perform a Google search for general queries, but now you ask ChatGPT for the same information. Similarly, instead of browsing through multiple websites to plan a trip, you simply ask Gemini to take the reins.
paragraph2: AI is clearly changing the way people interact with software and devices, and the latest example of this shift comes in the form of a new Adobe plugin for ChatGPT.For reference, this isn’t Adobe making its ChatGPT debut. The software-maker made Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Express, and Adobe Acrobat accessible within ChatGPT back in December last year. Today’s update significantly expands on that integration.With the Adobe plugin, ChatGPT users now have access to more than 70 tools across Adobe’s creative and productivity suites. The appeal here isn’t just the number of tools. It’s the fact that they’re all available under a unified plugin.
paragraph3: The newly-introduced plugin brings tools and capabilities from Adobe Express, Photoshop, Firefly, Premiere, Acrobat, Lightroom, Illustrator, InDesign, Stock, and more under one roof. “One unified Adobe plugin now takes you from idea to finished work in a single connected experience in ChatGPT,” writes the creative software giant.Essentially, what once needed you to juggle multiple integrations can now be done in one place without really needing to understand the complexities of Adobe’s ecosystem. Plus, you don’t need to know which Adobe app is the best suited for the task. ChatGPT will figure that out for you.For example, you can share your vacation photos with the AI tool and prompt it with something like “Batch edit these photos by adjusting color, lighting, and tone. Plus, generate a highlight video with key moments for Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.
paragraph4: ” In this case, the AI tool might use Lightroom and Photoshop for image editing and Premiere to turn said images into a short video clip.That’s just one possible use case. You’re free to use the tool for more professional use cases as well, like creating social media campaigns, brochures, presentations, PDFs, and more.Get started with Adobe tools in ChatGPT Head to ChatGPT on the web or the desktop app. Click on “Plugins” in the left-aligned toolbar. Search for “Adobe.” Install the one that reads “Adobe Design, combine, and edit,” as seen in the reference images below.
paragraph5: Sign in to your Adobe account or continue as a guest. Try the plugin! The plugin is rolling out globally today. It’s worth noting that you don’t need an Adobe account to get started. However, being signed in will unlock more skills, generative AI tools, and continuity.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: IPO-Bound LEAP India Nets ₹744 Cr From Anchor Investors
title_bn: IPO-Bound LEAP India Nets ₹744 Cr From Anchor Investors
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Ahead of the commencement of the bidding for its public issue on August 7, logistics tech platform LEAP India has…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe startup allotted 4.67 Cr equity shares to anchor investors at a price of ₹159 per share, the upper band of its price spectrum With this, LEAP India’s IPO is all set to open on August 7. The public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹480 Cr and an OFS component worth up to ₹2,000 Cr Of the total, 1.9 Cr shares, or 40.1% of the total anchor round, were picked up by one life insurance company and six domestic mutual funds via a total of 15 schemes Ahead of the commencement of the bidding for its public issue on August 7, logistics tech platform Leap India has raised ₹743.6 Cr from anchor investors. The startup allotted 4.67 Cr equity shares to anchor investors at a price of ₹159 per share, the upper band of its price spectrum. Of the total, 1.
paragraph2: 9 Cr shares, or 40.1% of the total anchor round, were picked up by one life insurance company and six domestic mutual funds via a total of 15 schemes. The domestic mutual funds that anchored the round included Axis Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal, Bank Of India, Groww, ITI, among others. Other investors who participated in the round included Morgan Stanley, JM Financial, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, BNP Paribas, Societe Generale, among others. This comes hours after LEAP India raised ₹371.3 Cr in a pre-IPO placement. According to a media advertisement, the company privately placed 2.3 Cr shares for cash at an issue price of ₹159 per share. The round saw participation from Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC’s subsidiary Gamnat, Dymon Asia Multi-Strategy Investment and cofounder Sunu Mathew.
paragraph3: While Gamnat was allocated 1.8 Cr shares totalling nearly ₹280 Cr, Dymon was allotted 31.4 Lakh shares for nearly ₹50 Cr. Promoter Mathew-backed Matyas Possessiones was lapped up 14.5 Lakh shares for ₹24 Cr. With this, LEAP India’s IPO will now go live on August 7 and close on August 11. The logistics tech startup’s public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹480 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) component worth up to ₹2,000 Cr. At the upper end of its ₹151 to ₹159 price band, the IPO will value the company at about ₹7,004.5 Cr (about $735 Mn).
paragraph4: Founded in 2013 by Sunu Mathew, LEAP India offers supply chain solutions for equipment pooling, returnable packaging, inventory management and movement, transportation and maintenance. It claims to have so far served more than 1,000 customers at the end of March 2026, including the likes of Coca-Cola, Marico, Panasonic, Haier and Daikin. During the fiscal, the food and beverages segment accounted for more than a quarter of its business, followed by automotive and ecommerce. On the financial front, LEAP India’s net profit zoomed 66% to ₹62.3 Cr in FY26 from ₹37.5 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, operating revenue zoomed 56.4% to ₹729.5 Cr from ₹466.
paragraph5: 5 Cr in FY25. At the end of March 2026, the company had 14.7 Mn assets, comprising 8.98 Mn pallets and 5.71 Mn containers. LEAP India supports its operations through a network of more than 29 warehouses and service centres, along with over 10,100 customer touchpoints.

title: Pre-modded 22GB RTX 2080 Ti cards surface on eBay for $500 as VRAM-hungry local AI fans chase down every spare FLOP — Hong Kong-based seller offers AI-friendly memory mod for a reasonable price
title_bn: Pre-modded 22GB RTX 2080 Ti cards surface on eBay for $500 as VRAM-hungry local AI fans chase down every spare FLOP — Hong Kong-based seller offers AI-friendly memory mod for a reasonable price
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Services have recently popped up that will double your RTX 2080 Ti's memory to 22GB, but if you don't have a card to spare, you can now get a pre-modded 22 GB 2080 Ti for $499 from eBay.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Future) The AI boom means that no matrix math FLOPS are disposable, and that means older Nvidia GPUs with Tensor Cores are getting a new lease on life. Services are popping up that will outfit your RTX 2080 Ti with 22GB of VRAM, doubling its original memory pool and making it more useful for modern LLM and diffusion workloads. If you’re hard up for compute and you don't have an RTX 2080 Ti to modify, however, eBay has just the thing. A Hong Kong-based seller will send you a pre-modded 22GB 2080 Ti in exchange for $499.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUsThe listing only promises that you'll receive a "Turbo," i.e.
paragraph2: , blower-style, RTX 2080 Ti with the 22GB mod. Don't get too picky about the particular brand of card you might receive, as the seller says: "The GPU brand could be Gigabyte, MSI, ASUS, Leadtek or others. It depends on what we have in hand."The eBay listing photos show a Gigabyte blower-style card along with a large box of presumably modified cards ready to ship and a GPU-Z screenshot confirming the availability of 22528 MB of memory from a running card.The seller only has 99.6% lifetime feedback on eBay, which is relatively low, but feedback for this specific listing shows that at least 38 happy buyers have received these cards and that they’re working as described.
paragraph3: Assuming you can count yourself as one of those happy buyers, a $500 22GB RTX 2080 Ti might be the best VRAM bang for your buck that you can find these days. That relatively large memory pool, combined with the RTX 2080 Ti's 616 GB/s of memory bandwidth and Tensor Cores, means that it's still useful for local LLM tasks, although its raw compute capacity and limited reduced-precision data type support compared to more modern products might make demanding diffusion workloads leisurely.Among Turing cards, the 24GB Titan RTX still commands about $800 on eBay at today's prices, and a Quadro RTX 6000 with the same amount of VRAM is about $900. The local AI enthusiast's favorite RTX 3090, which has 24GB of faster GDDR6X offering 936 GB/s of memory bandwidth, looks to be selling for about $1200. Ampere RTX Pro cards with even more VRAM rapidly get more expensive from there.The fact that all of these GPUs are still commanding such high prices many years after their introduction is a testament to the continuing utility and universal availability of Nvidia’s Tensor Core architecture across both consumer and data center products since 2018.
paragraph4: Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.AMD has had matrix math accelerators in its IP arsenal since CDNA 1 in 2020, but their availability has been limited to Instinct data center products until RDNA 4 arrived early last year. Intel included XMX matrix engines in the Alchemist architecture from the start in late 2022, but Arc graphics products have faced considerable challenges beyond the presence or absence of that capability. And Apple only just introduced Neural Accelerators to its GPUs with the M5 family.All that means that if you’re hard up for VRAM capacity and still need a decent amount of compute to go with it, a 22GB RTX 2080 Ti could be a compelling and relatively budget-friendly way to get there, and you get access to the entirety of the CUDA software ecosystem in the bargain. Not bad for an eight-year-old GPU that might have previously ended up in the e-waste bin by now.
paragraph5: Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds. As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.

If you’re hard up for compute and you don't have an RTX 2080 Ti to modify, however, eBay has just the thing. A Hong Kong-based seller will send you a pre-modded 22GB 2080 Ti in exchange for $499.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUsThe listing only promises that you'll receive a "Turbo," i.e.
bangla_paragraph2: , blower-style, RTX 2080 Ti with the 22GB mod. Don't get too picky about the particular brand of card you might receive, as the seller says: "The GPU brand could be Gigabyte, MSI, ASUS, Leadtek or others. It depends on what we have in hand."The eBay listing photos show a Gigabyte blower-style card along with a large box of presumably modified cards ready to ship and a GPU-Z screenshot confirming the availability of 22528 MB of memory from a running card.The seller only has 99.6% lifetime feedback on eBay, which is relatively low, but feedback for this specific listing shows that at least 38 happy buyers have received these cards and that they’re working as described.
bangla_paragraph3: Assuming you can count yourself as one of those happy buyers, a $500 22GB RTX 2080 Ti might be the best VRAM bang for your buck that you can find these days. That relatively large memory pool, combined with the RTX 2080 Ti's 616 GB/s of memory bandwidth and Tensor Cores, means that it's still useful for local LLM tasks, although its raw compute capacity and limited reduced-precision data type support compared to more modern products might make demanding diffusion workloads leisurely.Among Turing cards, the 24GB Titan RTX still commands about $800 on eBay at today's prices, and a Quadro RTX 6000 with the same amount of VRAM is about $900. The local AI enthusiast's favorite RTX 3090, which has 24GB of faster GDDR6X offering 936 GB/s of memory bandwidth, looks to be selling for about $1200. Ampere RTX Pro cards with even more VRAM rapidly get more expensive from there.The fact that all of these GPUs are still commanding such high prices many years after their introduction is a testament to the continuing utility and universal availability of Nvidia’s Tensor Core architecture across both consumer and data center products since 2018.

Intel included XMX matrix engines in the Alchemist architecture from the start in late 2022, but Arc graphics products have faced considerable challenges beyond the presence or absence of that capability. And Apple only just introduced Neural Accelerators to its GPUs with the M5 family.All that means that if you’re hard up for VRAM capacity and still need a decent amount of compute to go with it, a 22GB RTX 2080 Ti could be a compelling and relatively budget-friendly way to get there, and you get access to the entirety of the CUDA software ecosystem in the bargain. Not bad for an eight-year-old GPU that might have previously ended up in the e-waste bin by now.

title: Gains From Unexercised ESOP Buybacks Taxable As Capital Gains: ITAT
title_bn: Gains From Unexercised ESOP Buybacks Taxable As Capital Gains: ITAT
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that gains arising from the repurchase of vested, unexercised employee stock options…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe tribunal ruled that vested, unexercised ESOPs by itself cannot be treated as securities and hence cannot be taxed at a higher rate of salary perquisites The order further adds to a series of conflicting rulings around how ESOPs fit into the existing tax framework, even as new-age companies are increasingly using such schemes to hire and retain talent The ruling originated in a tax dispute involving a Flipkart executive who reported the repurchase of unvested and unexercised ESOPs under LTCG The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that gains arising from the repurchase of vested, unexercised employee stock options (ESOPs) are taxable under the long-term capital gains (LTCG) bracket rather than salary perquisites. Gains taxed under the LTCG regime generally attract a lower tax rate than income taxed as salary perquisites, potentially reducing the tax liability for employees. In India, LTCG are generally taxed at a flat rate of 12.5% without indexation for most assets. The Bengaluru bench of the appellate tribunal held that stock options remain a right to subscribe to shares at a future date, and hence cannot be treated by itself as “specified securities” for the purposes of Section 17(2)(vi) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. “We are of the considered view that till a ‘specified security’ comes into existence upon exercise of the stock option by the employee, no value can be assigned to it. Accordingly, in such a scenario, the question of taxability under the head ‘salaries’ does not arise,” the ITAT stated in its order.
paragraph2: It further noted that repurchase of unexercised options constitutes a transfer of capital assets, making any resulting gains eligible for taxation under Section 45 of the Act. The ruling, which came in last week, was related to a case involving a Flipkart senior executive. As per their income tax return, the executive reported a gross salary of ₹1.90 Cr along with LTCG of ₹2.45 Cr, including ₹2.33 Cr received after Flipkart repurchased 2,653 vested stock options. However, the assessing officer sought to reclassify the proceeds of the buyback as a salary perquisite under Section 17(2) of the Income Tax Act, subjecting it to higher income tax rates applicable to salary slabs.
paragraph3: Following an unsuccessful appeal with the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), the executive had approached the ITAT for relief. What Does The Ruling Entail? The ruling, while impactful, applies only to a narrow range of situations where ESOPs have not been exercised but have been vested and cancelled for a payment, said boutique tax consulting organisation Tax Compaas’ CEO Ajay Rotti. “I have mainly seen this happen in the past where a startup is acquired by a large company and the acquirer does not want to continue the ESOPs, or wants to replace them with their own options. In a small percentage of cases, the company may say I will cancel these options and I’ll give you money,” said Rotti. In situations where ESOPs are exercised, the difference between the strike price of the option and the fair market value would continue to be taxed as salary, he added. Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co’ partner (tax practice) Gouri Puri believes that the ruling could create a distortion in the tax treatment of two economically equivalent transactions .
paragraph4: She compared two situations where an employee granted ESOPs by their company had two options of exercising their options and selling the shares versus cancelling the options and receiving a payment in compensation. While the proceeds in the former scenario would be treated as a salary perquisite, in the latter scenario, they would attract taxation at the lower LTCG rate. However, Rotti noted that, doing so, was effectively giving up the commercial upside of ESOPs in order to bring down one’s tax burden. “As an employee, if I know that the company is going to do well and the share prices are going to go up, I will say I don’t care about the additional tax. I would want to hold the shares for more time,” he said. However, the ruling raises another question, according to Meyyappan Nagappan, partner at Trilegal. While companies typically report share buybacks as employee related expenses for tax purposes, the ruling implies that it should instead be treated as an acquisition of a capital asset.
paragraph5: “There might be a mismatch in how the company treats its expenses versus how the employee is taxed. The categorisation treatment has an implication on the various disclosures,” he added. In the bigger picture, while ESOPs are often a key means for startups and new-age companies to acquire and retain talent, how the ruling fits into the existing tax framework remains unclear. Notably, the Delhi, Karnataka, and Madras High Courts have all delivered conflicting rulings in other cases on similar questions of whether payouts for unexercised ESOPs should be taxed as perquisite. The recurrence of such cases only seems likely to increase as ESOP schemes are becoming all the more common. In 2025, over 9,200 startup employees unlocked a cumulative ₹1,409 Cr in liquidity through ESOP buybacks. Ultimately, these questions could remain a matter of contention unless policymakers or administrative authorities explicitly clear the air in the future.

title: Lok Sabha Passes Taxation Laws Amendment Bill, Clearing Path To Levy MDR On UPI Payments
title_bn: Lok Sabha Passes Taxation Laws Amendment Bill, Clearing Path To Levy MDR On UPI Payments
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Lok Sabha on Thursday (August 6) passed the bill amending the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe Lok Sabha on Thursday (August 6) passed the bill amending the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to further amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 Only a day ago, the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) governor Sanjay Malhotra mentioned that consumers have to ultimately pay for the transactions in some way or the other On social media platform X, Sitharaman said, MDR applies only on the merchants and not on the end users/customers The Lok Sabha on Thursday (August 6) passed the bill amending the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to further amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The amendments clear the path for the central government to introduce merchant discount rates (MDR) on UPI transactions. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced the bill to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, today in the Lok Sabha. Now, the bill will be proposed in the Rajya Sabha.
paragraph2: On social media platform X, Sitharaman said, “MDR applies only on the merchants and not on the end users/customers. It will support the banks and fintech to invest more on infrastructure, innovation & security. All users of UPI will reap the benefits of this investment.” She further added, “The UPI and Services Steering Committee headed by NPCI is yet to decide on the MDR.
paragraph3: This will happen after the Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposes to amend Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.” Only a day ago, the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) governor Sanjay Malhotra mentioned that consumers have to ultimately pay for the transactions in some way or the other. Meanwhile, the industry has been backing the reintroduction of the MDR on UPI. Yesterday, the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) showed its support for a nominal MDR on higher-value UPI transactions if proposed by the government.
paragraph4: As per reports, the government is expected to levy a 0.25-0.4% MDR on UPI transactions above ₹2,000 made to businesses. Meanwhile, normal, P2P transactions are likely to remain exempted.
paragraph5: UPI transaction volume saw a 4% monthly growth to 23.66 Bn in July, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), while the total transaction value increased 3% M-o-M to ₹29.88 Lakh Cr during the month under review.

title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’
title_bn: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Virginia's public utility regulator now requires all data center projects to pay for the infrastructure needed to supply their power. This makes it one of the first states to convert the 'ratepayer protection pledge' into an actionable policy.
paragraph1: The State Corporation Commission, Virginia’s independent state agency that regulates public utilities, has ordered data centers to pay for all the required transmission infrastructure that the project will use exclusively. According to Realtor.com, Governor Abigail Spanberger (D) has recently been pressing AI hyperscalers to reduce their impact on the power grid and utility prices.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centersVirginia currently has the greatest number of data centers across the U.S., with the state hosting at least 570 sites.
paragraph2: Because of the massive power demand of these sites, the state has been experiencing issues with electricity price hikes, with one county even asking its employees, including schools, to conserve power. PJM Interconnection, which distributes power to the state, has increased prices by 76%, with Monitoring Analytics, the independent watchdog keeping an eye on the utility company, saying that this is mostly due to AI data centers.The move requiring data centers to pay for their own upstream electrical infrastructure should, hopefully, ease the burden on the average Virginian. "We are taking real steps to address rising energy costs for Virginians," said Gov. Spanberger. "I will continue to work with the General Assembly and take action to make sure data centers pay their fair share, adhere to strict environmental standards, and listen to the concerns of local communities.
paragraph3: ”This is one of the first statewide announcements that will enforce President Donald Trump’s ratepayer protection pledge. Trump summoned the biggest AI hyperscalers to the White House in early March and made them promise that they will “pay their own way” when it comes to building the infrastructure they need. But despite this, the burden of more expensive electricity hasn’t eased for the average American. The administration expanded this promise in late July to include state governors, utility companies, and data center developers.Many critics said that this pledge is nothing but a piece of paper, with some comparing it to a “pinky promise.” After all, this is just a commitment and not a regulation that would penalize companies that don’t comply.
paragraph4: Nevertheless, it seems that it has spurred at least one state to make a move that should, hopefully, have a material impact on the average citizen.Aside from Virginia, Oregon is the only other state, so far, that has raised electrical rates for large consumers, like data centers. According to the Oregon POWER Act, facilities that consume 20 MW or more are assigned to a higher rate class. Portland General Electric, the state’s largest power supplier, has already implemented this, resulting in a 30% rate increase for these big power users, while also cutting residential costs by 1.3%.While the average consumer isn’t necessarily paying for the power that data centers consume, utility companies had to conduct massive grid upgrades to support the increased demand from these developments.
paragraph5: The utility companies then equally passed on all the necessary capital expenditure to all consumers, instead of just the data centers. By requiring data centers to spend on their own grid upgrades, further increases in electricity prices could, hopefully, be prevented.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds. Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.
